title: Deferred schema commit and tool-call snapshot recovery for streaming responses
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce deferred schema commit protocol for streaming responses to allow partial emits while preserving a final schema verification step; add compact snapshotting around function/tool calls so the runtime can replay and repair streamed tool-invocation payloads. No user-facing API breaking changes; default behavior behind feature flag 'deferred_schema_commit' and gated for OpenAI-compat mode.
description:
Motivation: Streaming structured outputs sometimes emit partial or malformed JSON fragments before the model settles on a final schema-compliant payload. When tool/function calls are interleaved in the stream, we observed unrecoverable toolcall payload corruption at the SDK/adapter boundary. This PR implements a deferred-schema-commit protocol plus lightweight snapshotting around function call boundaries to enable runtime repair and deterministic resume without dropping the stream or silently returning invalid tool payloads.

Design summary: We separate the streaming lifecycle into three phases: provisional emit, in-flight toolcall snapshot, and final schema commit. Provisional emits are allowed to stream token-by-token with permissive validation; when a function/tool call boundary is detected we capture a compact snapshot of the KV-cache + pending tokens and fence the toolcall path so the tool invocation payload can be constructed deterministically from the snapshot. After the model finishes, we perform a final schema commit check against the full reconstructed output. If commit fails, the runtime will attempt localized repairs (coercion, partial re-run of last segment, or graceful rejection) depending on the configured strictness level. This preserves streaming latency while providing actionable errors for strict mode.

Implementation highlights: - New protocol handshake on the response_format negotiation layer: client indicates willingness to accept deferred commits via response_mode: "deferred_commit" (OpenAI-compat shim maps "response_format.deferred_commit"). - Streaming runtime: implement SnapshotManager to capture compact state at tool boundaries; snapshots are persisted in-memory for short TTL and also emitted to the tracing pipeline for debugging. - Toolcall fencing: added deterministic serializer at the adapter layer to rehydrate tool payloads from snapshots; tool invocations now include a snapshot id and sequence anchor. - Schema verification: final schema commit uses the existing JSONSchema validator but with staged checks (soft-validate provisional segments, hard-validate on commit). Validation failures map to structured error codes (SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED, TOOLCALL_MISMATCH, SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED). - Config: feature flag "deferred_schema_commit" (off by default), strictness profile via existing response_schema_mode (per-request override).

Files changed (high-level): runtime/streaming/manager.py, runtime/streaming/snapshot.py, api/response_format/negotiator.py, adapters/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py, sdk/python/redwood/response.py, tests/streaming/test_deferred_commit.py, docs/api/response_formats.md. Diffs are intentionally small per file; most complexity is in snapshot and adapter code paths.

Testing & rollout: Unit and integration tests covering snapshot capture/replay, toolcall fencing, and final commit failure modes. Added e2e canary against hosted OpenAI-compat endpoint to validate expected behavior with sample tool-calling prompts. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, enable in staging for 48h, then gradual rollout to 10% of hosted traffic with monitoring for SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED and SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED rates; automatic rollback if error rates exceed thresholds.

Notes: This PR focuses on runtime and protocol; SDKs receive a minimal compatibility shim to surface structured error codes to callers. Followups will include telemetry dashboards for commit fidelity and UX improvements in the Console to surface snapshot traces for debugging.

review_conversation: Diego Marquez (2026-02-20): Can we avoid holding large KV caches in memory for long-running streams? Suggest bounding snapshot size and using a checksum to avoid reserializing identical state.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Addressed — SnapshotManager now trims and stores diffs; added checksum-based dedupe and TTL of 60s by default. See runtime/streaming/snapshot.py changes.
Lena Hoffman (2026-02-22): If the final commit fails in strict mode, what's the recommended SDK behavior? Do we return a partial result or an error code?

Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): For strict mode we return a structured error (SCHEMA_COMMIT_FAILED) and include last good snapshot id; SDKs will surface this as an exception with repair hints. For permissive mode we coerce and return best-effort payload and emit telemetry.
